title: The duality conjecture for metric entropy
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the duality conjecture for metric entropy: for all constants a, b >= 1 there are symmetric convex bodies K and a cube L with log N(K, L) > b log N(L°, a^{-1} K°); by polarity both inequalities of the conjecture fail. The first lesson proves the bipolar theorem, converts a real matrix into a pair of bodies, and proves the duality theorem for convexified packing of Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann. The second builds columns from partitions with few classes, with a logarithmic profile, and approximates all their combinations by a short list. The third proves the polynomial zero bound, chooses random directions for symmetric multilinear forms over a finite field, shows that the rows are separated, and proves the theorem and its consequence for convexified packing.
prerequisites: foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hahn-banach-baire-and-the-basic-theorems-on-banach-spaces (Theorems 6.2 and 6.3, separation of convex sets, used in R^n)
